legend: Keys got caught lacking, sleeping in English class, and was forcefully shaken awake by the teacher. (This would never have happened if Keys had instead slept in the sleeping bag.) As punishment, he was given this task to solve.

He was given an array of integers a$$$a$$$ of length n$$$n$$$. His goal is to find if he can sort the array using only valid swaps. Define a swap as valid if for the j$$$j$$$-th swap, elements ai$$$a_i$$$ and ai+1$$$a_{i + 1}$$$ are swapped, and min(ai,ai+1)≥j$$$min(a_i, a_{i + 1}) \ge j$$$.
Unfortunately, Keys enjoys sleeping in his sleeping bag too much to solve the problem. Please help solve the problem for him before he gets in trouble!
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤100$$$1 \le t \le 100$$$). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$).
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤109$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$).
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 105$$$10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, print YES if it is possible to sort the array; otherwise, print NO. You can output the answer in any case (upper or lower). For example, the strings "yEs", "yes", "Yes", and "YES" will be recognized as positive responses.
note: For the first test case, a valid sequence of swaps is the following: For the 1$$$1$$$-st swap, swap a1$$$a_1$$$ and a2$$$a_2$$$. This is valid since min(a1,a2)=1$$$min(a_1, a_2) = 1$$$, and 1≥1$$$1 \ge 1$$$. For the 2$$$2$$$-nd swap, swap a3$$$a_3$$$ and a4$$$a_4$$$. This is valid since min(a3,a4)=3$$$min(a_3, a_4) = 3$$$, and 3≥2$$$3 \ge 2$$$. After these two swaps, the array is sorted.
For the second test case, it can be seen that it is impossible to sort the array since the 2$$$2$$$ is not able to make it to the third position.
